claims.statement: Box documents an access token returned by its token endpoint as a bearer token (token_type bearer) with an expires_in lifetime in seconds, used to make authenticated API calls. Existence and lifecycle shape only: no prefix, alphabet or length is established.

sources.supports: A token that can be used to make authenticated API calls. (AccessToken); token_type: The type of access token returned. enum [bearer]; expires_in: The time in seconds by which this token will expire.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: The specification mentions an "app token" only as an accepted subject_token for token exchange and does not define it, and does not mention a developer token. Are app tokens and developer tokens distinct credential families with their own format or issuance, or the same access-token family obtained by another route? Needs the developer documentation (starting locator: app token with SDK guide), which was not readable.

Which prefix, alphabet and length, if any, does the provider state? The specification's example access-token value has a different shape from its example client secret and is not a format statement; no format claim is recorded.
Is a downscoped access token (issued_token_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token, restricted_to resources) a separate family or a scoped instance of this one?
